item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is closer to the contract and substantially more reviewable, though it still needs correction before merge. B explicitly expands retry/body-ownership behavior across RawClient and duplicates Files.Add instead of routing Upload through it.","reasons":["A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and keeps Files option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors centralized in a shared implementation.","B duplicates the complete Files.Add request/response path inside Upload, directly violating the requirement to route through FilesService.Add and increasing maintenance drift risk.","B introduces broad RawClient retry, Content-Length, seeking, and reader-ownership changes affecting Files.Update, Persons.AddPicture, and arbitrary callers, despite the contract forbidding unrelated retry refactoring.","A's retry test combines an open-file source, multipart field/name/content verification, a 429, and verification of identical content on the second attempt; this closely exercises the reported scenario and replayability requirement. A also tests lower-level Add retry behavior directly."],"risks_a":["A changes FilesService.Add by eagerly reading and buffering every custom multipart body, violating the requirement to preserve Add's existing behavior and potentially changing memory use, timing, reader-closing behavior, and error wrapping.","Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the public Add method, so it does not literally satisfy the required routing contract.","The patch has no visible explicit empty-filename or nil-content validation and adds no validation or failing-source-reader tests; correctness may depend on undocumented behavior of multipartbody.NewFile."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses Add and duplicates its option, request, response-decoding, and error logic.","The RawClient change is an out-of-scope behavioral refactor, including new seeking, Content-Length, retry, and Close semantics for all seekable request bodies.","The shared seekable reader is rewound and reused by GetBody, introducing mutable-reader coupling below the service layer and making the retry machinery harder to reason about safely or concurrently within the HTTP stack assumptions involved here relative to simple buffering at Upload construction time—as required by the contract and established helper pattern—and it changes ownership semantics by suppressing Close for caller readers, which is explicitly unrelated to the requested API change and can surprise existing callers relying on prior behavior despite preserving their file descriptor in this case; the test suite also omits the required source-reader-error case and its Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than combining retry with an open/streamed source."]}
